    <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","headline":"Wait until after GPS lock hold before updating position, if we can.","articleBody":"After the [recent patch](https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/pull/7801) , we hold lock for a bit before updating the position. The positions that come in after the hold are genuinely better positions than what we've been doing before. However, they only come 20 seconds after we've got lock. \n\nSo, at the moment, to avoid badness while making an improvement what the code is set up to do is update the local position twice - first, when lock is obtained, and second, after the hold expires. Since local position updates are asynch to mesh broadcasts, it means in many cases the good position will be broadcast, but not always.\n\nInstead, if the settings allow, we should skip that first local position update.\n\n\"If the settings allow\" is the meat if this issue. If we look at the broadcast/smart update/gps update intervals and they are all well above 20 seconds, it's likely safe. However, on the other end, we don't want to break GPS updates for the people who leave GPS permanently on (gps_interval \u003c10secs). We want to avoid potential loops where any of the broadcast/update/interval settings are set to exactly or less than the 20 second hold time. All doable, just needs some attention to detail.","author":{"url":"https://github.com/fifieldt","@type":"Person","name":"fifieldt"},"datePublished":"2025-09-18T22:57:58.000Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"https://schema.org/CommentAction","userInteractionCount":5},"url":"https://github.com/8029/firmware/issues/8029"}</script>

data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body NewMarkdownViewer-module__safe-html-box__ZT1eD"><p dir="auto">After the <a href="https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/pull/7801" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/meshtastic/firmware/pull/7801/hovercard" aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+ArrowUp">recent patch</a> , we hold lock for a bit before updating the position. The positions that come in after the hold are genuinely better positions than what we've been doing before. However, they only come 20 seconds after we've got lock.</p>
<p dir="auto">So, at the moment, to avoid badness while making an improvement what the code is set up to do is update the local position twice - first, when lock is obtained, and second, after the hold expires. Since local position updates are asynch to mesh broadcasts, it means in many cases the good position will be broadcast, but not always.</p>
<p dir="auto">Instead, if the settings allow, we should skip that first local position update.</p>
<p dir="auto">"If the settings allow" is the meat if this issue. If we look at the broadcast/smart update/gps update intervals and they are all well above 20 seconds, it's likely safe. However, on the other end, we don't want to break GPS updates for the people who leave GPS permanently on (gps_interval <10secs). We want to avoid potential loops where any of the broadcast/update/interval settings are set to exactly or less than the 20 second hold time. All doable, just needs some attention to detail.</p></div></div><div class="IssueBodyViewer-module__IssueBodyTaskList__a_Inr"><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 data-team-hovercards-enabled="true" class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body NewMarkdownViewer-module__safe-html-box__ZT1eD"><p dir="auto">OK, so here's how I think this is going to pan out:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table role="table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>gps_update_interval</th>
<th>Behaviour</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1-10 secs</td>
<td>No hold logic. Always update the local position. Accuracy comes from the fact the GPS is always on (see GPS::down() )</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>11-19 secs</td>
<td>Hold for (gps_update_interval – 1). Update local position after the hold. This gives the best possible chance for a high quality lock, given our limited hold time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>20 secs</td>
<td>As per 11-19 seconds (so hold for 19 secs)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21-40 secs</td>
<td>Hold for 20 seconds, and then update the local position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>41+ secs</td>
<td>As per 21-40 seconds.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Open Questions:<br>
0) Is 1 second tolerance enough? Should we hold</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Should there be different behaviour for chips that soft sleep vs those that hard sleep? Especially for the 11-19sec case, imagine if a soft-sleeped chip gets a lock that doesn't improve over the remaining hold since its ephemeris storage process is so good.</li>
<li>What happens if the position broadcast intervals are less than the gps_update_interval?</li>
<li>While we're holding is there some optimisation we can do to run the gps thread less often (without running out of buffer).</li>
<li>Is using 20 second hold even for an gps_update_interval of 40 seconds too aggressive? Should we water it down to reduce power usage at the expense of accuracy?</li>
<li>What happens if we lose lock during the hold time?</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Current Assumptions:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>The position we get at the end of the hold is more accurate than any position that came before it. So far this is true in T1000E testing, but may not be true on other chips.</li>
</ol></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><section aria-label="Events"><div (#8064)

* Wait until after GPS lock hold before updating position, if we can.

After the recent patch, we hold lock for a bit before updating the position.
The positions that come in after the hold are genuinely better positions
 than what we've been doing before. However, they only come 20 seconds
 after we've got lock.

Previously, we would update the local position as soon as we got a lock as well
as at the end of the hold, since a hold was not always possible.
With this patch, if the settings allow, we should skip that first local position update.

Fixes https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/issues/8029

* Fix falling edge handling.

* spelling

Co-authored-by: Copilot <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Congeal lock handling

* Add named constants

* define unit to avoid confusion

Co-authored-by: Copilot <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* ifdef, not if.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add handling for when we first turn on.

* Don't run if not active

* Reset fixhold

* Logic fixes

* Add path for ACTIVE--> IDLE --> ACTIVE

Previously we only covered HARDSLEEP --> ACTIVE.

* Change hold time to gps_update_interval - 10s

* Update comment

* Add extra buffer to avoid re-starting hold
